summary: This bash function wraps a Docker-based document converter tool. It checks that Docker is installed and that both the Docker image and a helper script exist before running the actual conversion; if anything is missing, it prints helpful instructions on how to set things up.

explanations.11: This creates a local variable that stores the Docker image name 'docling', making it reusable throughout the function instead of hardcoding it everywhere.
explanations.12: This expands the home directory (~) to its full path now and stores it in a variable, so the script can reference an absolute path later.
explanations.14: This tells the shell linter to ignore a warning on the next line because we intentionally want the ${HOME} to appear as literal text in messages, not be expanded.
explanations.15: This stores the path as it should appear in user-facing messages — with ${HOME} shown as-is rather than expanded, so users can copy the command regardless of their username.
explanations.19: This checks if the 'docker' command exists and is executable; the >/dev/null redirects suppress any output, and 2>&1 combines error and standard output.
explanations.24: This checks if either the helper script is missing OR the Docker image doesn't exist by trying to inspect it; if either check fails, we need to provide setup instructions.
explanations.43: This runs the actual conversion script with bash, passing through any arguments ($@) that were given to the function, like the filename to convert.
